text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CONGRESSMEN ACCUSED OF IRREGULAR ROLE IN AMAZON FUND

Brazil's Federal Accounts Tribunal, in a report approved this week, reaffirmed charges against senators and deputies accused of irregular participation in firms receiving incentives through the government's Amazon Investment Fund (Finam).
-- NICHOLAS BRADY WANTS TO INVEST IN LATIN AMERICA

Former U.S. Treasury secretary Nicholas Brady said his bond plan that helped rescue several debt-plagued Latin American nations is working, prompting a hunt for investment opportunities in the region.
-- BANKS EXPECT RECOVERY OF SAVINGS IN FOURTH QUARTER
Brazilian banks are working with the expectation that savings will recover in 1996's last quarter the 6.4 billion reais lost in the year's first nine months.
O GLOBO
-- RIO MAYORAL CANDIDATE FALLS IN POLLS TO 35 PERCENT
A poll said Rio de Janeiro mayoral front-runner Luiz Pedro Conde slipped three percentage points to 35 percent, adding that the Rio race is not expected to go to a second, run-off round of voting.
-- VIOLENCE KILLS 80, INJURES 1000 IN ISRAEL

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rushed back from an official trip to Germany to try to end two days of violence between Israelis and Palestinians that has so far killed 80 people and injured close to 1,000.
-- GENERAL STRIKE BRINGS ARGENTINA TO STANDSTILL AGAIN
Nearly all of Argentina's productive sector came to a stop yesterday at the start of a 36-hour general strike, the second in six weeks called to protest President Carlos Menem's economic policy.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- CONFLICTS IN WEST BANK KILL 50
Armed conflicts in West Bank and Gaza yesterday killed 39 Palestinians and 11 Israelis, prompting Israeli tanks to be put on the streets for the first time since the Six Day War in 1967.
-- BANK STRIKE ALTERS PAYMENT OF 24-HOUR CHECKS
The government, in response to the beginning of a nationwide bank strike, has provisionally raised from 130 rerais to 500 reais the minimum value of checks that must be paid in 24 hours.
-- COURT SUSPENDS COMPLAINT AGAINST GLOBO NETWORK
A Brazilian court has suspended a complaint against media giant Globo, accused of favoring government candidate Jose Serra in the race for Sao Paulo mayor.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
